primary_requirements_summary: Performance-sensitive Dedicated prospect. Target environment: H100 (prefers 8xH100 nodes; open to 4xH100 if throughput holds). Strong interest in FP8 attention + INT8 matmul for unit-cost improvement, but needs proof on realistic prefill/decode mixes. Asks repeatedly for reproducible benchmark methodology (clock pinning, driver/CUDA versions, warmup, variance/error bars) and clear interpretation guidance. Needs rollout safety plan (flags + perf canary + auto rollback) and a documented fallback policy by model/shape regime.
tech_notes: Key metrics Summit cares about: TTFT (p95) and TPOT (p95) under mixed workloads (tool-calling + long-context doc prompts). Their internal SLO language: 'no surprises' on p95 latency; willing to trade small p50 latency for stable p95. They asked specifically whether FP8 attention can regress TTFT due to launch overhead and whether scheduler knobs are required to realize gains end-to-end. They also asked if kernel selection is automatic by GPU arch/shape and what guardrails exist (unsupported shapes -> baseline).
model_and_workload_preferences: Interested in 'top hosted models' equivalents (they didn’t name a single model; they want the option to pin a version and have a safe quantized default). Workloads: (1) customer-support summarization (short decode, medium prompt), (2) RAG chat (long prompt, medium decode), (3) tool-calling agent (burst concurrency). They want the benchmark suite to include long-context distributions and structured output / function-calling variants.
